newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 25.

text.p: - An international body to oversee the decommissioning of paramilitary weapons is the key component of an agreement between Irish and British prime ministers John Bruton and Tony
- The top names in world fashion are expected to set up shop in a 20 million punt Irish "village".
- Fianna Fail leader Bertie Ahern is expected to take a decisive

step toward becoming prime minister by getting the agreement of an opposition deputy for the post of speaker of parliament. - The government has been warned that failure to decide within the next month on the funding and location of over 1,750 high-tech training places would be nothing short of disastrous

- British prime minister Tony Blair is expected to have a final consultation with Irish premier John Bruton this morning ahead of his eagerly-awaited Commons statement detailing his last chance offer to Sinn Fein to join the so-called settlement train.

- Fianna Fail has made considerable advances in its negotiations to secure majority support in parliament for the installation of a minority coalition government with the Progressive Democrats. - A major management reorganisation is being discussed at Fruit of the Loom in Donegal under which Willie McCarter may step down as chief executive.
- Finance minister Ruairi Quinn said the government may not have
to borrow any money this year.

- An effort by the British and Irish government to restart the peace process was heading toward failure last night as senior Unionists insisted they had not accepted the thrust of an Anglo-Irish decommissioning plan.

- Fianna Fail's hopes of securing the backing of the Green party for Bertie Ahern's bid to become prime minister were dashed last night after leading party figures agreed to vote against him tomorrow.
